model.name: Lifecycle / Status
model.purpose: Common state machine and effective validity for any host subject, covering discrete status, legal configurations, transitions, and the interval during which a status is valid in the world.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-021 is a format-neutral mixin that an adopting Dimension attaches to a host entity, event, relationship or artifact so that agents can understand, create, inspect and operate that host's discrete lifecycle status and its effective validity. It models the governing state machine, the current configuration, transition events and guards, valid-time versus record-time, unknown and error outcomes, replacement, and the authority and evidence required to change status. It does not own host identity, calendars, full process orchestration, full provenance graphs, retention schedules, or domain taxonomies of asset stages.
in_scope: Identity of a lifecycle binding, of a governing state machine, and of status codes, using master-system identifiers, governed IRIs, or Dimension-assigned UUID/ULID.
State-machine topology: atomic, compound, parallel and final states; history vertices; initial configuration; legal configurations.

Transition definition and execution: triggering events, guard conditions, internal versus external transitions, document-order selection, on-entry and on-exit effects, delayed events, and child-machine invoke.
Current runtime status and, for parallel regions, the active configuration as a set rather than a single token.
Canonical and resource-specific status codes, lifecycle pattern families, publication status versus process status, unknown, and entered-in-error as a non-deleting outcome.
Effective validity as a (possibly open) interval with inclusive bounds, future planned validity, and missing-end meaning ongoing.
Bitemporal split: valid time of the subject in the world versus transaction/record time of the observation or ingestion.
Temporal encoding with RFC 3339 timestamps including seconds and an explicit offset or Z, event time versus observation time, and optional temporal reference system.
Allen-style interval relations between validity intervals.
Transition audit, history restoration (shallow and deep), replacement and supersession, and terminal outcomes.
Authority, evidence and confirmation of a status, access consequences of status, and retention of status history as records.
Interoperability mappings onto canonical status codes without claiming lossless round-trip.
out_of_scope: Host identity, naming and identifier assignment for the subject itself, which belong to an identity sibling.
Calendar, clock, time-zone rule and temporal reference-system definition, which belong to a time sibling; this mixin only records which TRS a validity instant uses.
Full process, workflow, choreography or BPMN orchestration of work, which belong to a process sibling; SCXML/UML machines here are the status control abstraction, not a work-plan.
The complete provenance graph of all generations and derivations, which belongs to a provenance sibling; this mixin only records the activity that effected a status transition.
Physical or industry asset life-cycle stage taxonomies whose names ISO 55000 leaves to the organization.
Legal in-force status of instruments, licences or statutes, which belongs to a legal-status sibling.

Records retention schedule design, disposal authorities and legal hold policy, which belong to a records sibling; this mixin only records that status history is a record that must be kept as long as needed.
Technical resource versioning versus business versions as a versioning sibling, except to note that lifecycle is not a version identifier.
Spatial geometry and location models, except where a status is about entity availability of a located thing.
SQL:2011 APPLICATION_TIME and SYSTEM_TIME syntax, IEC 61512/ISA-88 equipment states, and Petri-net semantics, which were not taken as canonical for this mixin.

boundary_notes.distinction: A date is not an identifier. Status, validity start and validity end do not identify the host. Entered-in-error does not retire the host identifier. This mixin references the host; it does not assign host identity.

OWL-Time and RFC 3339 supply instants, intervals, durations and TRS. This mixin uses those primitives to state when a status is valid; it does not define calendars, leap-second policy, or local daylight-saving rules. RFC 3339 timestamps are instants and explicitly do not describe periods.

SCXML and UML state machines are a control abstraction for status. They are not a substitute for process models that plan work, allocate resources or choreograph participants. FHIR itself separates clinical workflow process, request/order fulfilment, entity availability and clinical interpretation.

A status change is an activity that generates or invalidates a status entity. The full influence graph, derivations and alternate-of relations belong to PROV. This mixin records the transition activity, agent, event time and observation time only.

FHIR distinguishes technical resource versions from business lifecycle. A new technical version may leave business status unchanged; a status transition may occur without a new business identifier. This mixin does not version content.

Status codes are a specialised classifier with modifier and legal-transition semantics. General type, kind and taxonomy membership belong to a classifier sibling. Canonical FHIR resource-status is an experimental mapping target, not a universal taxonomy.

Who may authorise a transition, who requested it, and who observed it are agent references. Agent identity and roles live in a party sibling; this mixin only records the association of an agent with a transition activity.

ISO 15489 requires records and their metadata to be created, captured and managed over time with assigned responsibilities. Status history is a record. Retention periods, disposal and legal hold are not defined here.
Whether a law, licence or contract is in force is a legal-status concern. Discrete operational status and valid-time intervals here do not decide legal force.

FHIR states there is no element on a resource that can convey whether it is on a current curated list; status=active is not membership. Current-list membership is a sibling relationship, not a status value.

sources.title: State Chart XML (SCXML): State Machine Notation for Control Abstraction
sources.relevance: Normative generic state-machine execution: states, parallel regions, transitions with event and cond, initial and final, onentry and onexit, history, legal configurations, events, IDs, and interpretation algorithm.

sources.title: Time Ontology in OWL
sources.organization: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) / Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC)
sources.relevance: Temporal entities, hasBeginning and hasEnd, hasTime, durations, TRS, xsd:dateTimeStamp, Allen interval relations, and documented PROV-O alignment. Effective validity is expressed with these primitives.

sources.title: FHIR Life Cycle Page (Resource Status, Current Lists, Entered in Error)
sources.version_or_date: FHIR R5 v5.0.0, 26 March 2023, Trial Use, Maturity 3
sources.relevance: Four lifecycle pattern families, entered-in-error without implied deletion, technical versus business versions, and the rule that current-list membership cannot be inferred from status.

sources.title: CodeSystem http://hl7.org/fhir/resource-status — Canonical Status Codes for FHIR Resources
sources.version_or_date: FHIR R5 v5.0.0, draft as of 2023-03-26, Experimental, Trial Use
sources.relevance: Master set of canonical status codes including error, proposed, planned, draft, requested, active, suspended, failed, replaced, complete, inactive, abandoned, unknown, unconfirmed, confirmed, resolved and refuted, used as an alignment target not a mandated vocabulary.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Status change as Activity; generatedAtTime and invalidatedAtTime; startedAtTime and endedAtTime; atTime on instantaneous events; wasAssociatedWith an Agent; wasGeneratedBy and wasInvalidatedBy.

sources.title: ISO 19108:2002 Geographic information — Temporal schema
sources.relevance: Normative emphasis on valid time rather than transaction time for temporal characteristics abstracted from the real world; basis for validity intervals of features, operations and metadata.

sources.title: DCMI Metadata Terms
sources.relevance: dcterms:valid as date or range of validity; dcterms:available; dcterms:issued and dcterms:modified; dcterms:replaces and dcterms:isReplacedBy; dcterms:accessRights; PeriodOfTime class.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.version_or_date: RFC 3339, July 2002, Proposed Standard; updated by RFC 9557
sources.relevance: Internet profile of ISO 8601 for instants with four-digit year, seconds, and explicit UTC offset or Z; unknown offset convention -00:00; periods are out of scope of this RFC.

sources.title: OMG Unified Modeling Language (UML) Version 2.5.1
sources.relevance: Normative UML state-machine metamodel that SCXML cites via Harel state tables. Clause 14 of UML is the abstract syntax that PSSM executes. Graphical UML is an alignment, not this mixin's storage format.

sources.title: Precise Semantics of UML State Machines (PSSM) Version 1.0
sources.relevance: Operational execution semantics for a large subset of UML 2.5.1 state machines as an extension of fUML, including semantic variation points for time sources. Used to ground transition effects without treating UML XMI as the mixin semantics.

sources.title: ISO 15489-1:2016 Information and documentation — Records management — Part 1: Concepts and principles
sources.relevance: Records, metadata, assigned responsibilities and processes for creating, capturing and managing records over time regardless of form. Status history is a record; retention duration itself is out of scope.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR R5 Period datatype (StructureDefinition)
sources.relevance: Normative time range with inclusive start and end; missing end means ongoing; start SHALL be less than or equal to end; start may be past and end future. Complements OWL-Time intervals for effective validity.

bundles.name: Mixin identity and host binding
bundles.description: How a lifecycle/status record is identified and bound to a host subject and to the machine and code system that govern it, without becoming the host's identity.
bundles.rationale: A mixin that cannot name its own record, its host, or its governing machine cannot be inspected or operated. SCXML requires IDs; FHIR requires resource identity distinct from status; DCMI and PROV identify the described entity separately from its validity or generation time.

layers.name: Lifecycle record identity
layers.description: Identifiers for the mixin instance itself and the priority order in which they are assigned and resolved.

findings.name: Lifecycle binding identifier
findings.description: Each attached lifecycle record has its own identifier, distinct from the host identifier and from any timestamp. SCXML 3.14 requires IDs on machine vertices; FHIR resource identity is separate from status; a date is not an identifier.

questions.text: What authoritative master-system identifier uniquely names this lifecycle binding, and which system is the master?
If no master-system identifier exists, what governed global IRI, or which Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID, identifies the binding?
Has any date, validity start, or observation time been incorrectly treated as the binding identifier?

data_elements.name: Lifecycle record identifier
data_elements.description: Primary identifier of this mixin instance, never a date.

data_elements.name: Identifier scheme
data_elements.description: Whether the identifier is a master-system key, a governed IRI, or a Dimension UUID/ULID.

data_elements.name: Identifier assignment time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant when the identifier was assigned; not itself an identifier.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The binding identifier is reference data carried on the mixin record; no separate artefact is required unless the master system issues a certificate or register extract.

findings.name: Host subject binding
findings.description: The mixin is meaningless without a host. FHIR status is a property of a resource; OWL-Time hasTime associates a temporal entity with anything; PROV generation times bound an Entity. The host is referenced, not copied.

questions.text: Which host subject does this lifecycle record describe, and by which identity priority is that host referenced?
Does the status apply to the whole host, to a stated aspect, role, or version of the host, or to a process the host represents?
May the same host carry multiple concurrent lifecycle bindings (for example workflow status plus clinical status plus publication status)?

data_elements.name: Host subject reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the identified host to which this mixin is attached.

data_elements.name: Status aspect
data_elements.description: Which facet of the host this binding governs, so concurrent machines do not collide.

data_elements.name: Host type
data_elements.description: Type or class of the host, for pattern selection, not a status code.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Host binding is a reference; the host artefact lives in the host model.

layers.name: Governing machine and code-system identity
layers.description: Which state machine and which status code system this binding is evaluated against.

findings.name: Governing state machine identifier
findings.description: SCXML documents declare an xmlns, version and initial state; UML state machines have a context classifier. The mixin must name the machine definition, its version, and its initial configuration independently of any XML or XMI projection.

questions.text: What identifier and version name the governing state machine definition for this binding?
What is the declared initial state or initial configuration of that machine?
Does this Dimension claim SCXML, UML/PSSM, or only a local machine profile, and is that claim evidenced?

data_elements.name: State machine reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the governing machine definition.

data_elements.name: Machine definition version
data_elements.description: Version of the machine definition, distinct from host business version.

data_elements.name: Initial state identifier
data_elements.description: Declared entry vertex of the machine.

artifacts.name: State machine definition
artifacts.description: The governed definition of states, transitions, guards and effects. Projection may be SCXML, UML, or another serial form; the semantics are the machine, not the file type.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system identifier of the machine definition; else a governed IRI for the definition; else a Dimension UUID/ULID. Version is not the identifier.

findings.name: Status code system binding
findings.description: Status values are codes from a named system. FHIR maps resource-specific required value sets onto experimental canonical resource-status. DCMI recommends controlled vocabularies. The mixin records the local system and any canonical mapping, and must not claim FHIR canonical codes as universal.

questions.text: Which code system and value set constrain the status codes used by this machine?
To which canonical status code, if any, does each local code map, and is that mapping lossy?
Does the bound code system include a first-class unknown (or equivalent) rather than allowing omission to mean unknown?

data_elements.name: Status code system
data_elements.description: URI or identifier of the local status code system.

data_elements.name: Status value set
data_elements.description: Constrained set of codes the machine may emit as current status.

data_elements.name: Canonical mapping reference
data_elements.description: Optional map from local codes to http://hl7.org/fhir/resource-status or another canonical set.

artifacts.name: Status code system
artifacts.description: Enumerated codes, definitions and any canonical map used by this machine.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Canonical URI of the code system if published; else master-system identifier; else Dimension UUID/ULID.

bundles.name: State machine specification
bundles.description: The definition of vertices, hierarchy, orthogonality, history, transitions and legal configurations that constrain runtime status.
bundles.rationale: SCXML, UML and PSSM agree that status is not a free token: it is a configuration of a machine with well-defined legal shapes, compound and parallel structure, and transition rules. Without the specification, a status code cannot be validated or progressed.

layers.name: Machine topology
layers.description: Kinds of states and how they nest, run in parallel, terminate, or remember prior configuration.

findings.name: States and vertex kinds
findings.description: SCXML distinguishes atomic states, compound states with children, parallel regions whose children are all active, final states that complete a region, and history vertices. UML adds pseudostate kinds executed by PSSM. A status token that ignores kind cannot represent parallel or nested machines.

questions.text: What states exist in the machine, and is each atomic, compound, parallel, final, or a history vertex?
What is the definition of each state in domain terms, and which host aspects may occupy it?
Are state identifiers unique within the machine, and what scheme assigns them?

data_elements.name: State identifier
data_elements.description: Unique identifier of a vertex within the machine.

data_elements.name: State kind
data_elements.description: atomic, compound, parallel, final, history-shallow, history-deep, or other declared kind.

data_elements.name: Parent state identifier
data_elements.description: Containing compound or parallel state, absent for top-level vertices.

data_elements.name: State label
data_elements.description: Human-readable name; not an identifier.

findings.inline_only_rationale: State vertices are part of the machine definition artefact already declared; they are inline members of that definition.

findings.name: Compound, parallel and final semantics
findings.description: When a compound state is active, exactly one child is active. When a parallel state is active, all children are active and process events independently. A final state completes its region; a top-level final completes the machine and yields a done event in SCXML. These rules make current status a configuration, not always a single code.

questions.text: For each compound state, which child is the default initial child, and must exactly one child be active?
Which regions are orthogonal, and is the current status therefore a set of active states rather than one token?
Which states are final, and what completion event or done data is produced when they are entered?

data_elements.name: Default child identifier
data_elements.description: Initial child of a compound or parallel region.

data_elements.name: Orthogonal region flag
data_elements.description: True when siblings are simultaneously active.

data_elements.name: Completion event
data_elements.description: Event raised when a final state is entered.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Compound, parallel and final rules are members of the machine definition artefact.

findings.name: History vertices
findings.description: SCXML history records the last active configuration of a compound state so that re-entry can restore shallow (immediate children) or deep (full descendant configuration) history. Absence of history means re-entry uses the default initial child. This is a rare but first-class lifecycle case.

questions.text: Does the machine declare shallow or deep history vertices, and for which compound states?
If no history has yet been recorded, which default transition does the history vertex take?
Is recorded history retained across suspend, invoke of a child machine, or only within a single run-to-completion cycle?

data_elements.name: History kind
data_elements.description: shallow or deep.

data_elements.name: History default target
data_elements.description: Target used when no history value exists.

data_elements.name: History retention scope
data_elements.description: How long and across which sessions the last configuration is kept.

findings.inline_only_rationale: History vertices are members of the machine definition; recorded history values at runtime belong to the transition-audit artefact.

layers.name: Transitions and legal configurations
layers.description: How the machine is allowed to move, and which sets of active states are legal.

findings.name: Transition definition
findings.description: A transition has a source, optional event descriptor, optional guard condition, optional target, optional executable content, and type internal or external. Eventless transitions fire when the condition is true. If several match, SCXML takes the first in document order. Unmatched events are discarded.

questions.text: What transitions are defined, including source, target, event, guard, type and order?
Which transitions are eventless, and what condition causes them to fire without an external event?
If no transition matches an event, is the event discarded, logged, or treated as an exception?

data_elements.name: Transition identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of a defined transition.

data_elements.name: Event descriptor
data_elements.description: Event name pattern that enables the transition; absent for eventless transitions.

data_elements.name: Guard condition
data_elements.description: Boolean condition that must hold for the transition to be selected.

data_elements.name: Transition type
data_elements.description: internal or external, controlling whether the source state is exited.

data_elements.name: Target state identifiers
data_elements.description: One or more target vertices.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Transition definitions are members of the machine definition artefact.

findings.name: Legal state configurations
findings.description: SCXML section 3.11 defines legal state configurations and specifications: not every set of states may be simultaneously active. Parallel regions require all children; compound states require exactly one child path to an atomic state. Runtime status that is not a legal configuration is invalid regardless of code-system membership.

questions.text: What rules determine whether a set of active states is a legal configuration of this machine?
If an observed configuration is illegal, is it rejected, repaired to the last legal configuration, or recorded as error?
When parallel regions are active, is the recorded current status the full configuration set, a projection to one canonical code, or both?

data_elements.name: Configuration rule
data_elements.description: A constraint on simultaneous active states.

data_elements.name: Illegal configuration policy
data_elements.description: reject, repair, or mark-error.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Legal-configuration rules are part of the machine definition; observed illegal configurations are recorded on the runtime status and audit artefacts.

bundles.name: Status classification and pattern families
bundles.description: Which family of lifecycle the host uses, which codes are allowed, and how special codes such as unknown, error, publication and clinical interpretation are distinguished.
bundles.rationale: FHIR shows that a single universal status list is neither the primary objective nor sufficient: work groups choose resource-specific required value sets, then optionally map them to an experimental canonical set. Mixing publication, process, entity-availability and clinical-interpretation codes without a pattern family causes false transitions.

layers.name: Lifecycle pattern families
layers.description: Named families of status value sets that are not interchangeable.

findings.name: Lifecycle pattern family
findings.description: FHIR documents four families: clinical workflow process (planned, in-progress, on-hold, stopped, completed, cancelled); request/order (proposed, draft, requested, rejected, accepted, in-progress, completed, cancelled); entity availability (draft, active, suspended, amended, retired); and clinical status (active, inactive, unknown) which is explicitly not a workflow lifecycle. ISO 15489 adds a records-management process family of create, capture and manage over time. The mixin must declare which family a binding uses.

questions.text: Which lifecycle pattern family does this binding use, and is more than one family attached to the same host via distinct aspects?
Which status codes are meaningless in this family and must be rejected (for example retired on a clinical-interpretation binding)?
If the family is clinical interpretation, has it been kept distinct from workflow or request status so that inactive does not mean completed?

data_elements.name: Pattern family
data_elements.description: workflow-process, request-order, entity-availability, clinical-interpretation, records-management, or local family.

data_elements.name: Family notes
data_elements.description: Local interpretation of the family and any deviations from the FHIR characteristic sets.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Pattern family is a classification field on the binding; characteristic code lists live in the bound code system artefact.

findings.name: Canonical status codes
findings.description: http://hl7.org/fhir/resource-status enumerates a master set including error, proposed, planned, draft, requested, received, declined, accepted, arrived, active, suspended, failed, replaced, complete, inactive, abandoned, unknown, unconfirmed, confirmed, resolved, refuted, differential, partial and several availability and device codes. FHIR states all status codes are mapped to one of these, but the code system is experimental and not ready for production. Alignment is optional and possibly lossy.

questions.text: What local status code currently applies, including its system, code, display and definition?
What canonical resource-status code, if any, is this local code mapped to, and is the map official, local, or absent?
If canonical FHIR resource-status is used as a production vocabulary, what evidence overrides its experimental and not-ready-for-production flags?

data_elements.name: Local status code
data_elements.description: The status token in the bound local code system.

data_elements.name: Canonical status code
data_elements.description: Optional map target in http://hl7.org/fhir/resource-status.

data_elements.name: Status display
data_elements.description: Human-readable display; not an identifier.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Codes are inline values whose definitions live in the status code system artefact.

layers.name: Special status codes
layers.description: Unknown, error, publication and confirmation codes that are often misused as ordinary workflow states.

findings.name: Unknown, error and modifier semantics
findings.description: unknown means the authoring system does not know the status. error / entered-in-error means the resource was created accidentally and should be ignored, but FHIR notes that in many cases the information cannot be removed. Artifact status in FHIR is a modifier because applications should not use a retired artefact without due consideration. Omission is not a substitute for unknown.

questions.text: When status is not known, is unknown recorded explicitly, and which agent and observation time support that assertion?
If the host was created in error, is entered-in-error (or error) set without deleting the record, and what redaction or notification is required?
Is this status a modifier that consuming applications must inspect before using the host?

data_elements.name: Unknown flag
data_elements.description: True when status is explicitly unknown.

data_elements.name: Entered-in-error flag
data_elements.description: True when the host or this status was created accidentally and must be ignored.

data_elements.name: Modifier flag
data_elements.description: True when consumers must not ignore this status.

data_elements.name: Error handling note
data_elements.description: Local rule for redaction, notification or retention when entered-in-error is set.

artifacts.name: Entered-in-error correction record
artifacts.description: Evidence that a host or status was created accidentally, the decision to mark error rather than delete, and any notifications.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system correction identifier; else governed IRI; else Dimension UUID/ULID. Event time and observation time are not identifiers.

findings.name: Publication status versus process status
findings.description: FHIR PublicationStatus (draft | active | retired | unknown) tracks artefact life-cycle of content, while process and request statuses track work. DCMI issued, available, modified and valid are publication and validity dates, not process states. Using draft both as unpublished content and as an unsent order collapses two machines.

questions.text: What publication status applies to the host if it is an artefact (draft, active, retired, unknown), distinct from any process status?
What issued, available, created, modified and valid dates are asserted, and which of them is validity rather than publication?
If publication status is retired, what due consideration is required before a consumer uses the host?

data_elements.name: Publication status
data_elements.description: draft, active, retired, or unknown for artefact hosts.

data_elements.name: Date issued
data_elements.description: Formal issuance instant or period.

data_elements.name: Date available
data_elements.description: Instant or period the host became or will become available.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Publication status and DCMI dates are inline fields; the artefact they describe is the host, not this mixin.

bundles.name: Runtime configuration and effective validity
bundles.description: The currently active configuration and the interval during which that status is valid in the world, plus the separate record of when that fact was observed or ingested.
bundles.rationale: ISO 19108 emphasises valid time. FHIR Period provides inclusive start and end with missing end meaning ongoing. OWL-Time supplies hasBeginning, hasEnd, hasTime and interval relations. RFC 3339 encodes instants, not periods. PROV separately timestamps generation, invalidation and observation. These axes must not be collapsed.

layers.name: Runtime configuration
layers.description: What is active now, including multi-state configurations and reasons.

findings.name: Current status value
findings.description: The status that currently applies. For a single-region machine this is one code; it remains a projection of the active configuration. Status reason, where used, explains suspended, failed, declined or similar without replacing the code.

questions.text: What is the current local status code, and at what event time did it become current?
What reason, if any, explains the current status (for example why suspended or declined)?
As of a stated instant, which status applied, and is that answer taken from valid time rather than record time?

data_elements.name: Current status
data_elements.description: Current local status code.

data_elements.name: Status reason
data_elements.description: Coded or textual reason for the current status.

data_elements.name: Status reason text
data_elements.description: Narrative reason when no code is available.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Current status and reason are inline runtime fields; their change history is the transition-audit artefact.

findings.name: Active configuration set
findings.description: SCXML configuration is the set of active states. Parallel regions make a single status code insufficient. The mixin records the full set and optionally a projected code for interchange.

questions.text: Which states are currently active, and is that set a legal configuration?
What single status code is projected from the configuration for systems that cannot represent a set, and is that projection lossy?
Are any child machines invoked from the current configuration, and what is their session identity and status?

data_elements.name: Active state identifiers
data_elements.description: Set of currently active vertices.

data_elements.name: Projected status
data_elements.description: Optional single-code projection of the configuration.

data_elements.name: Invoked sessions
data_elements.description: Child machine sessions started from current states.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The active configuration is runtime reference data; child machine definitions are separate artefacts already in scope.

layers.name: Effective validity
layers.description: Valid-time interval, record-time, encoding and interval relations.

findings.name: Valid-time interval
findings.description: dcterms:valid is a date often a range of validity of a resource. FHIR Period is a time range with inclusive start and inclusive end; if end is missing the period is ongoing; start SHALL be less than or equal to end; start may be in the past and end in the future. OWL-Time TemporalEntity has hasBeginning and hasEnd. Planned FHIR statuses describe a still-future course of action, so validity may start in the future.

questions.text: When does this status become valid in the world, is the bound inclusive, and may it be in the future?
When does this status cease to be valid, is the bound inclusive, and if end is absent is the period ongoing?
If both start and end are present, is start less than or equal to end, and which temporal reference system applies?

data_elements.name: Valid start
data_elements.description: Inclusive beginning of valid time, RFC 3339 with seconds and offset or Z when an instant is used.

data_elements.name: Valid end
data_elements.description: Inclusive end of valid time; absent means ongoing.

data_elements.name: Valid ongoing flag
data_elements.description: True when no end is known or the period is still open.

data_elements.name: Valid start inclusive
data_elements.description: Whether the start bound is inclusive; FHIR Period start is inclusive.

artifacts.name: Validity declaration
artifacts.description: Declared effective validity interval for a status binding, including bounds, ongoing flag and TRS.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identifier of the status binding plus valid-start; if those collide, a Dimension UUID/ULID for the declaration. Dates alone are not identifiers.

findings.name: Transaction time versus valid time
findings.description: ISO 19108 emphasises valid time rather than transaction time because it abstracts temporal characteristics from the real world. PROV still requires generatedAtTime, invalidatedAtTime and activity start/end. RFC 3339 timestamps protocol events. The mixin records event time of the real-world status change separately from observation or ingestion time. SQL bitemporal APPLICATION_TIME versus SYSTEM_TIME is an unadopted alignment, not a claim of this model.

questions.text: At what event time did the status actually change in the world, with seconds and explicit offset or Z?
At what observation or ingestion time was that change recorded, and which agent recorded it?
If valid time and record time disagree (late entry, planned future, correction), which axis is authoritative for which query?

data_elements.name: Event time
data_elements.description: When the status change occurred in the world.

data_elements.name: Observation time
data_elements.description: When the change was observed or ingested.

data_elements.name: Generated at time
data_elements.description: PROV generatedAtTime of this status entity.

data_elements.name: Invalidated at time
data_elements.description: PROV invalidatedAtTime when this status entity ceased to apply as a record.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Bitemporal instants are inline on the status record and on the transition-audit artefact; they are not a separate document.

findings.name: Temporal encoding and reference system
findings.description: RFC 3339 requires four-digit years, a stated relationship to UTC, and seconds; Z denotes offset 00:00; -00:00 means UTC time known but local offset unknown. OWL-Time prefers xsd:dateTimeStamp, allows other TRS including Unix-time and geologic time, and notes its encodings ignore leap seconds that ISO 8601 mandates. PSSM notes implementations may have a single centralised time source. Unqualified local time is not interoperable.

questions.text: Do all recorded instants conform to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z?
Which temporal reference system is used for each instant or interval, and is it Gregorian-UTC or another TRS?
If UTC is known but local offset is not, is -00:00 used rather than Z, and is unqualified local time forbidden?

data_elements.name: Temporal reference system
data_elements.description: TRS used for validity and event times.

data_elements.name: Timestamp profile
data_elements.description: Declared profile, normally RFC 3339 / xsd:dateTimeStamp.

data_elements.name: Leap-second policy
data_elements.description: Whether leap seconds are represented; OWL-Time encodings ignore them.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Encoding and TRS are parameters of timestamp fields, not a standalone artefact.

findings.name: Interval topology
findings.description: OWL-Time implements Allen's interval relations: before, after, meets, met-by, overlaps, overlapped-by, starts, started-by, during, contains, finishes, finished-by, equals, plus in and disjoint. These are required to compare successive validity intervals, detect illegal overlap of exclusive statuses, and relate a query instant to a validity period. IANA link relations exist for the interval relations.

questions.text: What Allen relation holds between this validity interval and the previous and next intervals for the same host aspect?
May two non-identical statuses of the same aspect have overlapping valid times, or must they meet or be disjoint?
Does a stated query instant fall during, before, or after the validity interval?

data_elements.name: Relation to previous interval
data_elements.description: Allen relation to the prior validity interval of the same aspect.

data_elements.name: Overlap policy
data_elements.description: Whether exclusive statuses may overlap in valid time.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Interval relations are computed or asserted properties of validity declarations, not a separate artefact.

bundles.name: Transition execution, history and terminal outcomes
bundles.description: How status changes are triggered, selected, executed, provenanced, restored, replaced, and brought to terminal outcomes including entered-in-error.
bundles.rationale: SCXML and PSSM define selection and execution order (exit, transition content, enter). PROV records the activity and agent. FHIR and DCMI model replacement and error. History vertices restore prior configuration. Without this bundle an agent can read status but cannot operate it.

layers.name: Transition execution
layers.description: Events, guards, delayed sends, and entry/exit effects.

findings.name: Triggering events and guards
findings.description: Events may be internal, external, delayed (SCXML send), or completion events from final states. Guards are conditions evaluated at selection time. SCXML processes internally enabled transitions before waiting on the external queue. Invoke starts a child session; finalize processes returned data.

questions.text: What event, including delayed or completion events, is proposed to trigger a transition, and is it internal or external?
Does the guard evaluate to true in the current datamodel, and which data did that evaluation depend on?
If the trigger is delayed, what delay or absolute time was requested, and can it still be cancelled?

data_elements.name: Event name
data_elements.description: Name of the triggering event.

data_elements.name: Event origin
data_elements.description: internal, external, delayed, or completion.

data_elements.name: Guard result
data_elements.description: Last evaluated guard outcome.

data_elements.name: Delay until
data_elements.description: Absolute RFC 3339 time at which a delayed event should fire.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Event and guard evaluations are captured on the transition-audit artefact when a transition is attempted or taken.

findings.name: Entry, exit and transition effects
findings.description: Taking transition T from S1 to S2 executes onexit of S1, then T's executable content, then onentry of S2. External transitions also exit and enter intermediate ancestors relative to the least common compound ancestor. Effects may assign data, raise events, send, log, or invoke. They are part of operating the mixin, not a general process model.

questions.text: Which onexit actions must run, and in what order, for the states being left?
Which executable content is attached to the transition itself, and did it succeed?
Which onentry actions must run, including default initial children down to atomic states, and what side effects are expected on the host?

data_elements.name: On-exit actions
data_elements.description: Executable content run on leaving a state.

data_elements.name: On-entry actions
data_elements.description: Executable content run on entering a state.

data_elements.name: Transition actions
data_elements.description: Executable content on the transition.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Action lists are part of the machine definition; their execution results are written to the transition-audit artefact.

layers.name: History, replacement and terminal outcomes
layers.description: Audit of transitions, restoration, supersession, error and completion.

findings.name: Transition audit and provenance
findings.description: Each taken or rejected transition is an Activity associated with an Agent, with atTime, startedAtTime and endedAtTime, generating a new status entity and invalidating the previous. ISO 15489 requires capture of records and metadata with assigned responsibilities. Event time and observation time are recorded separately.

questions.text: Which agent performed or authorised the transition, on whose behalf, and under which role?
What are the activity start, end and event atTime, and the observation/ingestion time of the audit record?
If the transition was not taken, was it because of a failed guard, illegal configuration, insufficient authority, or unmatched event, and was that recorded?

data_elements.name: Transition activity identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the PROV Activity that attempted or took the transition.

data_elements.name: Associated agent
data_elements.description: Agent associated with the activity.

data_elements.name: From configuration
data_elements.description: Active state set before the transition.

data_elements.name: To configuration
data_elements.description: Active state set after a taken transition.

data_elements.name: Transition outcome
data_elements.description: taken, rejected, or cancelled.

artifacts.name: Transition audit record
artifacts.description: Evidence of an attempted or taken status transition, including agent, times, from/to configurations, event, guard result and outcome. This is a record in the ISO 15489 sense.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system audit identifier; else governed IRI; else Dimension UUID/ULID. Event time is not the identifier.

findings.name: History restoration
findings.description: Re-entering a compound state with a history vertex restores the last recorded configuration (shallow or deep) instead of the default initial child. This is the rare resume-where-left-off case used after suspend, on-hold, or invoke return.

questions.text: What last configuration is stored for each history vertex, and when was it captured?
On re-entry, should history be restored or the default initial child used, and who decides?
If the machine definition changed since history was captured, is restoration forbidden?

data_elements.name: Stored history configuration
data_elements.description: Last active child set for a history vertex.

data_elements.name: History captured at
data_elements.description: When the configuration was stored.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Stored history values are inline runtime data; capture events are rows in the transition-audit artefact.

findings.name: Replacement and entered-in-error
findings.description: FHIR replaced means information was replaced by another resource; DCMI replaces / isReplacedBy model supersession. entered-in-error is usually not a clinical workflow state but applies to request and entity-availability cycles; handling is business-specific and there are no generic rules for redaction. Replacement is a relationship plus a status, not a silent overwrite.

questions.text: If this status or host is replaced, which resource or binding supersedes it, and is the inverse isReplacedBy asserted?
Is the host entered-in-error, replaced, retired, or inactive, and why is that distinction required for consumers?
Must the erroneous or replaced record be retained for integrity or digital signatures even though it must be ignored?

data_elements.name: Replaced-by reference
data_elements.description: The binding or host that supersedes this one.

data_elements.name: Replaces reference
data_elements.description: The binding or host this one supersedes.

data_elements.name: Retain for integrity
data_elements.description: True when deletion is forbidden despite error or replacement.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Replacement links are references; the entered-in-error record artefact already covers accidental creation.

findings.name: Terminal outcomes
findings.description: Characteristic terminal codes include complete/finished, failed/stopped/aborted, abandoned, declined, cancelled, retired, inactive and resolved/refuted. A top-level SCXML final generates a done event and ends interpretation. Terminal does not imply deletable. Abandoned is usually a workflow error distinct from successful complete and from failed.

questions.text: Is the current configuration terminal for this machine, and which terminal kind applies (complete, failed, abandoned, cancelled, retired)?
Is any further action planned, or has the process stopped with no further action planned?
May a terminal status be left (for example retired to active, or complete to in-progress), and under which transition and authority?

data_elements.name: Terminal flag
data_elements.description: True when no further automatic progress is defined.

data_elements.name: Terminal kind
data_elements.description: complete, failed, abandoned, cancelled, retired, or other declared kind.

data_elements.name: Further action planned
data_elements.description: False for FHIR complete, failed, abandoned and similar.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Terminal flags are inline runtime fields derived from the configuration and code system.

bundles.name: Governance, quality, access and interoperability
bundles.description: Who may change status, on what evidence, who may see it, how long status history is kept, and how it is mapped across systems.
bundles.rationale: ISO 15489 assigns responsibilities and records controls. PROV associates agents. DCMI accessRights describes security status of access. FHIR requires due consideration for retired and has no generic error-handling rules. Canonical mapping is experimental. These are operating questions, not boilerplate.

layers.name: Authority, evidence and access
layers.description: Authorisation, confirmation quality and access consequences of status.

findings.name: Transition authority
findings.description: ISO 15489 requires assigned responsibilities. PROV wasAssociatedWith and actedOnBehalfOf record who acted. Not every agent may take every transition; draft to requested, or active to retired, typically need different authority. The mixin records the required role or rule, not a complete IAM model.

questions.text: Which role or permission is required to take this transition, and which agent actually requested it?
Is the transition a records-management action that must be captured with metadata under assigned responsibility?
If authority is missing, is the transition rejected and audited, or queued for approval as proposed or requested?

data_elements.name: Required role
data_elements.description: Role needed to execute the transition.

data_elements.name: Responsible party
data_elements.description: Party assigned responsibility for this status record.

data_elements.name: Authority basis
data_elements.description: Policy, delegation or instrument that authorises the change.

artifacts.name: Transition authorisation
artifacts.description: Evidence that a named agent was authorised to take a status transition, including role, basis and time.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system authorisation identifier; else governed IRI; else Dimension UUID/ULID.

findings.name: Evidence, confirmation and quality
findings.description: Canonical codes include unconfirmed, confirmed, refuted, resolved, differential and partial. Clinical status is about how evidence affects interpretation, not workflow. Quality of a status assertion includes whether it is approved, ruled out, or still being assembled. PROV hadPrimarySource and qualified generation support evidence.

questions.text: Is the current status unconfirmed, confirmed, refuted, or still partial, and what evidence supports that?
What is the primary source of the status assertion, and was it derived from another status record?
If evidence conflicts (differential, refuted versus confirmed), which status is displayed and which is retained?

data_elements.name: Confirmation code
data_elements.description: unconfirmed, confirmed, refuted, resolved, differential, partial, or local equivalent.

data_elements.name: Evidence references
data_elements.description: Supporting observations, tests or documents.

data_elements.name: Primary source
data_elements.description: PROV hadPrimarySource of the status entity.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Confirmation and evidence are references and codes on the status record; the evidence documents themselves belong to other models.

findings.name: Access and exceptions by status
findings.description: dcterms:accessRights describes who may access a resource or its security status. Retired, entered-in-error, draft and unknown each imply different consumer behaviour. FHIR says applications should not use a retired artefact without due consideration. Exceptions include break-glass, research-only, and redacted error records. Spatial location of access is out of scope except as a policy parameter.

questions.text: Given the current status, who may read, transition, or export this binding by default?
If status is retired, error, or draft, what warning or block is presented to consumers?
Does entered-in-error or another status require redaction of payload while retaining the status history for integrity?

data_elements.name: Access rights
data_elements.description: Statement of who may access the host or status given current status.

data_elements.name: Consumer warning
data_elements.description: Required warning for retired, error, draft or unknown.

data_elements.name: Redaction applied
data_elements.description: Whether payload redaction accompanied a status such as entered-in-error.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Access implications are policy attributes of status; access-control systems are a sibling. Warnings are inline.

layers.name: Retention and interoperability
layers.description: How long status history is kept and how status is mapped across vocabularies and machines.

findings.name: Retention of status history
findings.description: ISO 15489 applies to creating, capturing and managing records over time regardless of form. FHIR notes erroneous information often cannot be removed for integrity. Status history, including error marks, is a record. The duration of retention is a records-sibling decision; this mixin only records the requirement to keep history and any hold.

questions.text: Must prior configurations and transition audits be retained even after a terminal or error status, and under which records policy?
Is hard deletion of a status record permitted, or only logical error/inactive marking?
Is a legal or audit hold preventing disposal of this status history, and who placed it?

data_elements.name: Retain history
data_elements.description: Whether transition history must be kept.

data_elements.name: Deletion policy
data_elements.description: forbidden, logical-only, or permitted-under-policy.

data_elements.name: Disposal hold
data_elements.description: True when disposal is suspended.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Retention flags are inline; the retention schedule itself is a sibling records artefact and is out of scope.

findings.name: Interoperability mappings
findings.description: FHIR maps resource-specific required value sets to canonical resource-status but says consistency is not the primary objective and the canonical system is experimental. SCXML, UML/PSSM and local machines are alignments, not identical semantics. dcterms:valid literals are not FHIR Period objects. Claims of conformance require evidence. Device-specific codes such as transduc-discon are not general.

questions.text: Which concept map, if any, is used to translate local status to a partner vocabulary, and what is its version?
Which local distinctions are lost in the map (for example abandoned versus failed versus cancelled), and is that acceptable to both parties?
Is any conformance to SCXML, UML/PSSM, FHIR lifecycle, OWL-Time or ISO 19108 claimed, and where is the evidence?

data_elements.name: Concept map reference
data_elements.description: Map used for interchange of status codes.

data_elements.name: Conformance claims
data_elements.description: Named specifications this binding claims to follow, each requiring evidence.

data_elements.name: Lossy distinctions
data_elements.description: Local codes that collapse under the chosen map.

artifacts.name: Status concept map
artifacts.description: Documented mapping between local status codes and one or more partner or canonical vocabularies, including lossy notes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Canonical URI of the map if published; else master-system identifier; else Dimension UUID/ULID.

functions.name: Bind lifecycle mixin
functions.description: Attach a lifecycle binding to a host with a governing machine, code system, pattern family and identifiers.
preconditions: Host identity exists in the identity sibling.
Machine definition is identified and has a legal initial configuration.
effects: Creates a lifecycle record bound to the host.

functions.name: Instantiate machine
functions.description: Enter the initial configuration, run onentry actions down to atomic states, and record observation time.
effects: Sets runtime configuration to the declared initial states.

functions.name: Select enabled transitions
functions.description: Given an event or empty event, evaluate guards in document order and return the enabled transition set without executing it.
preconditions: Machine is instantiated and not exited.
effects: None on configuration; may produce an audit of unmatched events if policy requires.

functions.name: Execute transition
functions.description: Exit source states, run transition content, enter targets, update configuration and project current status.
preconditions: Event time and observation time are RFC 3339 instants.

functions.name: Evaluate validity at instant
functions.description: Decide whether a status applied at a query instant on the valid-time axis, using inclusive bounds and ongoing-if-missing-end.
outputs: Allen relation of instant to interval
preconditions: Query instant uses RFC 3339 with offset or Z.
Caller states which time axis is intended.

functions.name: Map to canonical status
functions.description: Translate a local status code through a concept map to a canonical or partner code, recording lossiness.
preconditions: No silent claim that FHIR resource-status is production-ready.

functions.name: Mark entered in error
functions.description: Set error or entered-in-error without deleting the host, record the correction, and apply any redaction or notification policy.
preconditions: Deletion is not used as a substitute when integrity requires retention.
effects: Sets modifier status so consumers ignore the host.

functions.name: Restore history configuration
functions.description: On re-entry of a compound state, apply stored shallow or deep history instead of the default child.
preconditions: Stored configuration is compatible with the current machine version.
effects: Replaces default initial entry with stored configuration.

functions.name: Supersede status record
functions.description: Assert replaces / isReplacedBy, set replaced or retired as required by the pattern family, and keep the old record.
effects: Does not delete the superseded record.

functions.name: Validate legal configuration
functions.description: Test whether a proposed active set is a legal SCXML/UML configuration and whether start is less than or equal to end for validity.
effects: Read-only unless invoked as a pre-condition of execute-transition.

functions.name: Record transition provenance
functions.description: Create a PROV Activity for a transition attempt with agent, times, used event and generated status entity.
preconditions: Agent is identified in the party sibling or as a local agent reference.
effects: Adds an audit artefact that is a record under ISO 15489 principles.

composition.target: Host entity, event, relationship or artefact in the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Attach common state machine and effective validity to any host without becoming that host's identity or type.
Reuse instants, intervals, durations and TRS; do not redefine calendars or leap-second policy.
Treat each status change as an Activity that generates and invalidates status entities, with agents and times.
Keep work-plan orchestration in a process sibling; this mixin only executes the status control machine.
Host and binding identifiers come from the identity sibling; timestamps are not identifiers.
Status vocabularies and concept maps are specialised classifiers with transition constraints.
Transition authority, responsibility and observation agents are party references.
Status history is a record that must be captured and managed; disposal schedules remain in the records sibling.
Technical versions are not business lifecycle; do not encode status as a version number.
Operational status and valid time do not decide legal force of instruments.
Primary alignment for machine topology, events, guards, history, parallel regions and interpretation.

composition.target: OMG UML 2.5.1 state machines and PSSM
composition.purpose: Abstract syntax and operational semantics for Harel state machines; not an identity of SCXML XML.

composition.target: HL7 FHIR lifecycle and canonical resource-status
composition.purpose: Pattern families, entered-in-error, Period bounds and optional canonical mapping; experimental flags preserved.
Prefer valid time for real-world effectiveness; keep transaction time on a second axis.
Literal validity dates, availability and supersession relations as metadata alignment.
Current curated membership is not a function of status and must not be inferred from active.

owner_package_requirements: A designated governance steward owns the Dimension package that adopts WM-XCT-021 and names the master systems for lifecycle record identifiers, machine definitions and status code systems.

The package SHALL declare which lifecycle pattern families are permitted, which local code systems are bound, and whether any map to http://hl7.org/fhir/resource-status is used in production despite its experimental flag.
The package SHALL declare the timestamp profile (RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset or Z), the default TRS, and the policy that event time and observation time are stored separately.
The package SHALL name the records policy that retains status history and forbids silent deletion of entered-in-error records.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Place mixin instance IRIs under the adopting Dimension's governed namespace. Align temporal terms with http://www.w3.org/2006/time# when OWL-Time is used, PROV terms with http://www.w3.org/ns/prov#, DCMI validity with http://purl.org/dc/terms/valid, and optional canonical status codes with http://hl7.org/fhir/resource-status without importing FHIR resource identity. Machine vertex identifiers are unique within a machine, not globally, unless a governed IRI is assigned.
registry_links: Adopting Dimension registry of machine definitions and status code systems
Optional alignment registers for FHIR resource-status, SCXML documents and UML state machines

canonicalization_rules: Canonical timestamps are RFC 3339 date-time with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z; four-digit years required; unqualified local time is rejected; -00:00 is reserved for unknown local offset.
Canonical current status for interchange is the local code plus optional mapped canonical code; the local code remains authoritative.
A current configuration is canonicalised as a sorted set of state identifiers unique within the machine; a single projected code is an optional derivative.
Valid-time intervals canonicalise missing end as ongoing; if both bounds exist, start SHALL be less than or equal to end; bound inclusivity is explicit.
Replacement is canonicalised as a pair of references (replaces and isReplacedBy), not as in-place overwrite.
patch_rules: Status patches are transitions: a patch MUST name the event or explicit transition, the authorising agent, event time and observation time.
Direct overwrite of current-status without a transition audit is forbidden except for correcting transcription errors that themselves produce an entered-in-error or replacement record.
Validity bounds may be patched only by invalidating the previous validity declaration and generating a new one with provenance.
Machine definition patches produce a new machine version; in-flight bindings MUST record whether they stay on the old version or migrate.
compatibility_rules: Adding states or transitions is backward compatible if existing legal configurations remain legal.
Removing or renaming a state that appears in stored history is a breaking change.
Changing pattern family of an existing binding is a breaking change.
Maps to canonical resource-status MAY be added without breaking local codes; removing a local code is breaking.
Claiming new conformance to SCXML, UML/PSSM or FHIR requires evidence; silent tightening of guards is breaking for operators.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier of the lifecycle record, machine definition, audit event or code system.
Governed global identifier or IRI when the artefact is published across Dimensions.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension when neither master nor IRI exists. Dates, valid-start and observation time MUST NOT be used as identifiers.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All event times and observation or ingestion times use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; record both axes when they can differ.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artefacts use the artefact type, master or Dimension identifier, and an opaque serial component; do not embed status codes or dates as the unique name.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Transition audits, entered-in-error corrections and superseded records SHALL remain retrievable for integrity even when consumers must ignore the host; silent deletion is not a substitute for error status.

policies: Every status change is a recorded transition with agent, event time and observation time; unmatched or unauthorised attempts are audited.
unknown and entered-in-error are first-class; omission does not mean unknown; error does not mean delete.
Valid time answers what was true in the world; record time answers what the system knew when. Queries MUST name the axis.
Canonical FHIR resource-status and SCXML/UML alignments are optional; production use of experimental vocabularies requires an explicit Dimension decision.

read: Any authorised reader of the host may read current status, configuration, validity interval and consumer warnings.
Transition audits and evidence are readable by auditor and steward roles; redacted error payloads remain redacted.
As-of reads MUST specify valid-time or record-time axis.
create: Create is bind-lifecycle-mixin plus instantiate-machine, producing an initial configuration and observation time.
Create of a transition audit occurs only as an effect of execute-transition, mark-entered-in-error, restore-history-configuration or supersede-status-record.
update: Update of current status occurs only through execute-transition or the specialised error, history-restore and supersede functions.
Update of validity replaces the previous declaration with provenance; it does not rewrite history in place.
Update of machine definition is a new version, not a silent mutation of in-flight bindings.
delete: Hard delete is forbidden while retain-history is true or a disposal hold is set.
Logical delete is expressed as entered-in-error, retired, inactive or replaced according to pattern family.
Physical disposal, if ever allowed, follows the records sibling policy, not this mixin.

roles.name: Governance steward
responsibilities: Own the Dimension package, permitted pattern families, timestamp profile and whether experimental canonical maps are used.
Designate master systems for identifiers and machine definitions.

roles.name: Machine author
responsibilities: Define states, transitions, guards, history and legal configurations.
Version machine definitions and declare breaking changes.

roles.name: Transition operator
responsibilities: Submit events and request transitions within assigned roles.
Supply event time when known and never treat dates as identifiers.

roles.name: Status auditor
responsibilities: Read transition audits, unmatched events, unauthorised attempts and entered-in-error records.
Verify that event time and observation time are both present where required.

roles.name: Records officer
responsibilities: Ensure status history is captured as records with assigned responsibility.
Apply disposal holds and forbid silent deletion.

roles.name: Interoperability mapper
responsibilities: Maintain concept maps and lossiness notes.

access.default_rule: Default deny on transition execution; read of current status follows host read permission unless status is entered-in-error or retired, in which case a consumer warning is mandatory and payload may be redacted.
exceptions: Break-glass read of redacted error records by an auditor with recorded justification.
Machine authors may read machine definitions they do not operate.
Public artefacts with publication-status active may expose publication status without exposing transition audits.
audit_requirements: Every execute-transition, rejected transition, mark-entered-in-error, restore-history-configuration and supersede-status-record SHALL write a transition audit with agent, event time and observation time.
Reads of redacted error records SHALL themselves be audited.

read_order: AGENTS.md bootstrap contract for this Dimension package
Machine definition identified by Specification URL
Status code system and any concept map
Current lifecycle bindings and transition audits via Interface URL
Process descriptions at Processes URL for allowed transitions

coverage.claim: This mixin covers the defensible operating surface of discrete lifecycle status and effective validity as a format-neutral attachment: machine topology and legal configurations (SCXML/UML/PSSM), pattern families and codes (FHIR, with experimental flags preserved), valid time versus record time (ISO 19108, OWL-Time, FHIR Period, RFC 3339, PROV), transition provenance (PROV, ISO 15489), and replacement, unknown and entered-in-error. It does not claim a universal status vocabulary, SQL bitemporal conformance, asset-stage taxonomies, or legal in-force semantics.

checklist.notes: Binding, host, machine, state, activity and artefact identifiers with master/IRI/UUID priority; dates forbidden as identifiers.
Pattern families, configurations, transitions, history restoration, terminal kinds, publication versus process, reactivation rules.
Host binding, replacement/isReplacedBy, invoked child sessions, interval relations, agent associations, concept maps.
Valid interval, ongoing end, future planned start, event versus observation time, RFC 3339 encoding, TRS, Allen relations, delayed events.
Transition activity, generatedAtTime, invalidatedAtTime, associated agent, primary source, audit artefact.
Assigned responsibility, associated agent, on-behalf-of, required roles; party identity remains a sibling.
Legal configurations, Period start<=end, guard evaluation, machine-version compatibility for history, timestamp profile checks.
Status-dependent read/transition rules, retired/error warnings, redaction, break-glass exception.
Status history as records; error does not delete; disposal hold; hard delete policy deferred to records sibling.
Optional canonical map, lossiness, SCXML/UML/FHIR/OWL-Time/ISO 19108 alignments without unearned conformance.
Atomic, compound, parallel, final, history, internal/external transitions, document order, invoke.
Valid time as first-class interval with inclusive bounds and ongoing-if-missing-end.
Non-deleting error outcome with correction artefact and integrity retention.
Current status as a set when orthogonal regions are active, with optional lossy projection.
Location models are out of scope; FHIR Location.status is only an example of entity-availability, not a spatial geometry.

known_omissions: SQL:2011 APPLICATION_TIME and SYSTEM_TIME were not fetched as primary text and are not claimed.
IEC 61512 / ISA-88 equipment and batch states, ISA-95, and Petri-net semantics are uncovered.
ISO 55000:2024 asset life-cycle stage naming (organisation-defined) was seen only in secondary samples and is not canonical here.
RFC 9557 updates to RFC 3339 (time-zone suffixes) were not incorporated beyond noting the update.
BPMN 2.0 token state versus SCXML configuration is referenced as a sibling, not modelled.
Fuzzy, probabilistic or interval-valued uncertain validity has no primary support in the cited sources.
Saga/compensating-transaction status and two-phase commit states are omitted.
Legal hold procedures beyond a boolean flag belong to records/legal siblings.
Device-specific FHIR codes (transduc-discon, hw-discon) are not generalised.
Full SCXML datamodel, ECMAScript profile and HTTP event I/O processor are execution-environment details, not mixin semantics.
ISO 19108 TM_Period inner UML could not be quoted from the paywalled full text; only the official abstract (valid time versus transaction time) is used.
conflicts: FHIR says consistency of status codes across resources is not the primary objective, yet publishes an experimental canonical map that is not ready for production.
ISO 19108 emphasises valid time; PROV and RFC 3339 emphasise event/transaction timestamps; both axes are required and must not be collapsed.
RFC 3339 describes instants only; FHIR Period, OWL-Time and dcterms:valid describe intervals, with dcterms:valid as a literal rather than a structured period.
OWL-Time encodings ignore leap seconds; ISO 8601 mandates them.
OWL-Time 2022 is a Candidate Recommendation Draft; a 2017 Recommendation exists. Align to the cited 2022 CRD without claiming W3C Recommendation status for that edition.
SCXML XML, UML graphical/XMI and PSSM operational semantics are related Harel descendants, not identical.
Clinical status is not workflow status; using one code list for both is a conflict with FHIR.
Current-list membership cannot be inferred from status=active.
entered-in-error should be ignored but often cannot be removed, conflicting with naive CRUD delete.
RFC 3339 -00:00 (unknown offset) is semantically distinct from Z.
regional_assumptions: Default TRS is Gregorian calendar with UTC offsets as in RFC 3339 and xsd:dateTimeStamp; other TRS are allowed but not defaulted.
Canonical status tokens cited from FHIR are English codes; local systems may use other languages or jurisdictions.
Healthcare-shaped pattern families are alignments, not a requirement outside clinical Dimensions.
Records retention durations and legal holds are jurisdiction-specific and not specified here.
Daylight-saving and political offset changes are out of RFC 3339 scope; scheduled local wall-clock transitions need a time sibling.
adversarial_checks: Treat any proposal that uses a date as the lifecycle identifier as invalid.
Reject models that store only one timestamp for a late-entered historical status.
Reject single-code current status as complete when the machine has parallel regions.
Reject inference that status=active means membership of a current curated list.
Reject unstated production use of experimental http://hl7.org/fhir/resource-status.
Reject collapse of clinical-interpretation inactive with workflow completed.
Reject unqualified local times without offset or Z.
Reject silent overwrite of status without a transition audit and agent.
Reject claims of universal completeness of any status vocabulary.
